_note: Product-by-product fire evidence for the public table on /advice/wallcovering-fire-ratings-uk/. One row per product or product family, never per brand. classificationRaw is the fire line as printed; notation is the class copied from it (null when two documents disagree); classification repeats only what the notation prints. Rows were selected from the research records in docs/research/fire-ratings/manufacturers/ (checked 15 Oct 2026); see that folder for every product examined.

products.product: Fabric-backed vinyl, Type II, 460 gsm (woven and non-woven backings)
products.scope: The two 460 gsm Type II product types listed in the declaration. No product codes or colourways are listed; Muraspec says the product code is on the packaging.
products.construction: Vinyl on woven or non-woven fabric backing, Type II
products.classificationRaw: B-s2, d0 on fibre cement board attached with Murabond heavy adhesive

testedBuildup.other: No primer, lining, air gap or fixing is stated.

limitations: The class is declared only for the fibre-cement and Murabond Heavy build-up.

The declaration lists a notified-body certificate of conformity for each of these two product types (0493-CPR-W051, woven; 0493-CPR-W052, non-woven), with printed expiry dates of 28 October 2027 and 25 November 2027.

Muraspec's May 2026 hanging leaflet (p. 1) requires Murabond Sealed Surface adhesive on non-absorbent walls and a coat of Murabond Primer on absorbent walls (diluted 1:3 on uncoated plaster, plasterboard and MDF; 1:1 on emulsion-painted walls). Neither is part of the declared fibre-cement and Murabond Heavy build-up.
conflicts: Muraspec's earlier declaration CPR0002 (September 2024) declares B-s1,d0 for Type II non-woven fabric-backed vinyl; this 2025 declaration gives B-s2,d0.
unresolved: The classification report behind the declaration is not published.

Muraspec has published two documents under the number CPR0003 (version 1, September 2024, BTTG; version 4, July 2025, Centexbel) with different scopes, and whether version 4 replaces version 1 is not stated.

The BS 476 Class 0 and Class 1 statement is a British national classification, not a European class, and does not convert to one. England's Approved Document B dropped national reaction-to-fire classes from 2 March 2025 (transitional arrangements apply); the Welsh and Northern Irish guidance still print them.
The sheet says these designs can also be printed on other Tektura wallcoverings. The fire line does not say it covers those bases, so check the rating of the base actually ordered.
unresolved: What "suitable substrate" means.

The page also links Vescom's Protect family declaration DOP-CPR-01002 (July 2017: B-s2,d0 for cotton-backed vinyl with Vescom Protect, 370–480 g/m²) and certificate 0493-CPR-W015, stated valid 'latest on July 31st 2023'. The MPA Dresden classification behind it (20180730/01, Pleso + Protect) is limited to the tested 356 g/m² and 0.31 mm and excludes gypsum boards. No Protect test at about 460 g/m² was found.

conflicts: The report linked from the product page (CREPIM DO-18-0159\A-R1, 'VESCOM - RAINY') never names Colour Choice or Protect. It is one of the two reports behind Vescom's non-Protect vinyl family certificate 0493-CPR-W014, not a Protect-specific test.
unresolved: Whether Vescom holds a classification of Colour Choice+Protect at about 460 g/m² with the Protect laminate, and whether certificate W015 was renewed after July 2023.
Whether the linked report, printed as valid for five years from August 2018, has been renewed.

products.fieldOfApplication: Substrates of at least 1,800 kg/m³, at least 8 mm thick, A2 or better, excluding paper-faced plasterboard; primed with ET Primaseal at 85 g/m² and hung with Dixon Turner Heavy at 200 g/m² (as the field of application states); no variation in thickness, weight, composition or construction.
limitations: Paper-faced plasterboard is expressly excluded.
The report dates from 2012 and cites the 2007+A1:2009 edition of EN 13501-1; it is not invalid for that reason alone, but ask Newmor whether it remains the current evidence.
conflicts: The report names a Light grade of adhesive in the product description and a Heavy grade in the field of application.
